title: Base change under flat finitely presented morphisms with geometrically reduced fibres
statement:
Consider a Cartesian square of schemes [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square]
\[
\begin{array}{ccc}
X&\xleftarrow{h}&Y\\
f\downarrow&&\downarrow e\\
S&\xleftarrow{g}&T
\end{array}
\qquad Y\cong X\times_S T.
\]
Assume that $f$ is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism], locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], and each scheme-theoretic fibre $X_s$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre] is geometrically reduced over $\kappa(s)$ [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]. For every abelian sheaf $F$ on $T_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves], the canonical base-change morphism
\[
\beta_F:f^{-1}g_*F\longrightarrow h_*e^{-1}F
\]
is an isomorphism. Here inverse and direct images are those of [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] and [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. The morphism is the underived exchange [def-weil-pbc-underived-exchange] on the square with the horizontal and vertical sides exchanged: it is the adjoint under $h^{-1}\dashv h_*$ of $h^{-1}f^{-1}g_*F\cong e^{-1}g^{-1}g_*F\xrightarrow{e^{-1}\varepsilon_g}e^{-1}F$. There is no restriction on $g$ and no torsion hypothesis on $F$.

proof.text: Let U_Z forget abelian sheaves on Z to sets. Finite-limit preservation of set inverse image is supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-algebraic-structures]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-abelian-lift-hom] to f and e, obtaining comparison isomorphisms ef:U_X L_f^a ≅ L_f U_S and ee:U_Y L_e^a ≅ L_e U_T with their hom-set comparison equations. Apply the equation for e to the identity of L_e^a F. Naturality of the set homEquiv and ee inverse followed by ee give U_T(η_e^a) followed by R_e(ee_F) = η_e at U_T F.

source.place: Tag 00YV; abelian inverse image and underlying-set adjunction compatibility

proof.text: Let β be the specified abelian exchange. Apply the injective set adjunction bijection for f to (ef inverse at R_g^a F) followed by U_X(β) followed by R_h(ee_F). The f hom-set comparison identifies its first part with U_S applied to the abelian adjunct of β. The proved library identity unit_map_baseChangeMap_app in the module of [def-weil-pbc-underived-exchange] expresses that adjunct as R_g^a(η_e^a) followed by the direct-image square comparison. The latter is the composite of the two pushforward composition isomorphisms [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition]; after forgetting, its maps on sections are definitionally the same set restriction maps. Naturality moves R_f R_h(ee_F) to the front as R_g R_e(ee_F), and the unit identity of the preceding step replaces the resulting composite by R_g(η_e). This is exactly the set adjunct of setBaseChangeArrow, whose definition is pullback of this map followed by the f counit. Injectivity proves that the conjugated forgotten β equals setBaseChangeArrow.

source.place: Tag 0EZR, canonical base-change map by units, pushforward composition and counit; the iterated mate formula is already proved in BaseChange/Square.lean

proof.text: Apply [sbc-lem-degree-zero-flat-base-change] with the given square, the exact given flatness, local finite presentation and geometrically reduced fibre hypotheses, and the sheaf U_T F. The identified conjugated forgotten β is therefore invertible. Both comparison factors are isomorphisms, so cancellation of these factors gives invertibility of U_X(β). The forgetful functor on abelian sheaves reflects isomorphisms: the inverse of each bijective additive component is additive, and its naturality follows by cancellation. This is the Mathlib instance for sheafCompose applied to the forgetful functor from abelian groups. Hence β is an isomorphism. No new hypotheses on g or F enter.
